rationale: Verified two ways, not just the builder's self-report. (1) Code read of wardrobe.controller.ts/service.ts/repository.ts: every query scoped by userId from @AuthContext(); create sets user_id from the authenticated caller; findByIdForUser requires both id and user_id (findFirst); findManyByUserId filters by user_id. Re-ran the wardrobe test files independently: 12/12 passing. (2) REAL live black-box HTTP verification once both couture-cast builders were done and a server could be started without interference: started apps/api on a dedicated port with TEST_ENV=local (enables this codebase's own test-auth-bypass convention, test-token:<role>:<userId>) against the shared local Supabase Postgres. First attempt used synthetic user ids not present in the User table and got a 500 (Prisma P2003 foreign-key violation) — traced this to my own test setup, not the feature: GarmentItem.user_id is a real FK to User, and my synthetic ids weren't real rows. Retried against actually-seeded users (guardian-1, guardian-2) and got clean results: POST creates (201), GET list as guardian-1 shows it, GET list as guardian-2 is empty, GET by id as guardian-1 returns 200, GET by id as guardian-2 returns 404 'Garment not found'. All four Eval Contract behaviors (B-001 through B-003, plus the cross-user 404) hold under genuine live HTTP exercise, not just mocked tests. Worth recording as a methodology note: the first 500 would have been a false-positive 'defect' if I hadn't checked whether it was a real fault or a test-setup gap — exactly the discipline an evaluator (self or independent) needs to apply before reporting a finding. One judgment call worth surfacing, not a defect: category defaults to 'uncategorized' when omitted (CC-4.2's tagging work is explicitly out of scope).
